Theorem
[Uniqueness]

↗ thm:strong-maximum-principle-laplace

1. ch2:2.2-thm-5\group Maximum Principles

For $g\in C(\partial U)$ and $f\in C(U)$, there is at most one $u\in C^2(U)\cap C(\overline U)$ satisfying \[ (17)\qquad \begin{cases} -\Delta u=f& \text{in }U,\\ u=g& \text{on }\partial U. \end{cases} \]
Proof

\sketch The difference of two solutions is harmonic and vanishes on $\partial U$. Apply the maximum principle to the difference and its negative.

□
